meta.title: TrekLink: off-grid communication and node rental for trekking agencies
meta.description: TrekLink rents LoRa mesh nodes to registered trekking agencies on monthly or day plans, with one platform for the live map, tiered alerts, contracts and invoices on routes beyond phone coverage.

hero.sub: TrekLink owns and maintains a fleet of LoRa mesh nodes. Registered agencies rent them on monthly or day plans, collect them at our counter, and follow their groups on a live map with tiered alerts and invoices in one place.

problem.heading: On multi-day routes, your groups go days without signal
problem.without.label: Without TrekLink
problem.with.label: With TrekLink
problem.a.without: Groups are out of coverage for days, and the office hears from them when they walk out.
problem.a.with: Rented nodes pass position, status and SOS across the group over LoRa, and the Field Station uploads them when it has internet.
problem.b.without: An agency that wants its own off-grid devices has to buy and maintain them itself.
problem.b.with: TrekLink owns and maintains the nodes. You rent them on a monthly or day plan and collect them at our counter.
problem.c.without: Tracking and alerting depend on someone reaching a phone signal.
problem.c.with: One platform holds the live map, the tiered alerts, the contracts and the invoices for every rented node.
renting.heading: From registration to the returned node
renting.lede: Every step runs in the operations platform, and the nodes change hands only at TrekLink's counter.
renting.a.title: Register
renting.a.body: Your agency or company registers with its tax code. TrekLink verifies it before it can rent.
renting.b.title: Choose a plan
renting.b.body: Your manager picks a monthly or day plan and the number of nodes, then requests a contract. TrekLink approves it and issues the first invoice.
renting.c.title: Collect at the counter
renting.c.body: Once the first payment is confirmed, your manager signs the handover at TrekLink's counter and takes the nodes, set up for your organization.
renting.d.title: Follow the group
renting.d.body: The platform shows your rented nodes on a live map. An alert goes to your operators on duty, then your manager, and reaches TrekLink staff only if nobody acknowledges it.
renting.e.title: Return and settle
renting.e.body: Bring the nodes back to the counter when the plan ends, and pay the invoice online or at the counter.
how.heading: From a press on the ridge to your operator on duty
how.diagram.label: A terrain map with a mesh of trekker nodes, one guide's node and a Field Station. An SOS from one node ripples outward through every link until it reaches the Field Station.
how.a.title: Raise it
how.a.body: Press the SOS button on v1 or v2. On v3 and v4, hold the button for three seconds.
how.b.title: It spreads
how.b.body: Nodes in range repeat it, so it can ripple through the group and around gaps in coverage.
how.c.title: The Field Station uploads it
how.c.body: The Field Station, a laptop with one node on USB, queues the SOS and uploads it to the operations platform when the laptop is online. The alert then goes to your operators.
nodes.heading: Four iterations, one firmware
nodes.lede: Each version fixed what the last one taught us. All four run the same TrekLink mesh firmware, set per board at build time.
nodes.carousel.label: Node versions
nodes.renders: Product images are renders created from photographs of our prototypes.
node.v1.name: v1
node.v1.body: A perfboard build that proved mesh, GPS and fall detection work together. Mesh only, with no cloud uplink.
node.v1.alt: Render: TrekLink v1 prototype in a grey enclosure with a small OLED screen and a square SOS button
node.v2.name: v2
node.v2.body: The first purpose-built board and the first with a compass. Syncs to the cloud over MQTT.
node.v2.alt: Render: TrekLink v2 in its enclosure, with a blue-framed OLED screen and a round metal button
node.v3.name: v3
node.v3.body: A LilyGO T-Beam with GPS on board. SOS is a deliberate three-second hold, so a pocket can't send one.
node.v3.fall: No, the board has no motion sensor
node.v3.alt: Render: TrekLink v3 in a slim ribbed case with a small screen and an antenna
node.v4.name: v4
node.v4.body: The pocket-safe hold from v3, with fall detection back, a real-time clock and a microSD slot.
node.v4.alt: Render: TrekLink v4 in a slim ribbed case with a centred screen and an antenna

faq.heading: Before you rent
faq.a.a: Registered organizations: trekking agencies and companies, not individuals. An organization registers with its tax code, and TrekLink verifies it before its manager can request a contract.
faq.b.a: Two kinds. A monthly plan renews term by term until your manager gives notice. A day plan covers a set number of days. Current prices are on the plans page of the operations system.
faq.c.q: What happens if nobody acknowledges an alert?
faq.c.a: It escalates. The alert goes to the operator on duty, then to the backup operator, then to your organization's manager, and if nobody acknowledges it, to TrekLink staff. TrekLink does not replace official search-and-rescue channels.
faq.d.q: Do the groups need a SIM, a phone plan or internet on the route?
faq.d.a: No. Nodes talk to each other directly over LoRa. Only the Field Station laptop needs internet, and only to upload what it has queued.
faq.e.q: Which radio band does it use?
faq.e.a: Nodes default to the MY_433 region, 433.0 to 435.0 MHz, the band set for Vietnam and Malaysia.
cta.heading: Rent the fleet for your next group
cta.body: The plans page lists the monthly and day plans. Register your organization there to request a contract.

mesh.heading: Built on open-source mesh firmware with a worldwide community
mesh.body: TrekLink's firmware builds on Meshtastic, the open-source LoRa mesh project started in 2020. The radio layer is public code with a large community behind it. TrekLink adds the safety layer on top.
mesh.add.a: Store and forward: an event raised in a dead zone waits on the node until a link returns.
mesh.add.b: Fall detection that asks the carrier before it alarms, on v1, v2 and v4.
mesh.add.c: An SOS that stays open until a responder closes it, even after the buzzer is silenced.
